meta.disclaimer: This is a curated briefing prepared from public Microsoft sources. It is not a contractual roadmap, availability commitment, or licensing statement, and it is not an official Microsoft or Farmers Insurance publication. Verify current status, licensing and regional availability with Microsoft before making decisions.

relevanceAreas.name: AI grounded in trusted enterprise data
Cross-platform data access and reduced duplication
Security, governance, reliability and cost management

methodology: Started from the Azure blog hero post and followed its links to the workload blogs (Analytics, Power BI, Fabric Apps, OneLake, Real-Time Intelligence and IQ, Platform, SQLCon) and the September 2026 Fabric and Power BI feature summaries.

Each announcement records the status exactly as the source words it. Where a source says only “preview”, it is recorded as Public preview. “Announced”, “coming soon” and “available now” are never treated as equivalent.

Status was cross-checked against Microsoft Learn “What’s new in Microsoft Fabric” on the research cutoff date. Where sources disagree, the more conservative status is used and the discrepancy is shown on the card.

Items come from two evidence tiers: “Event blog” (named in the hero post or a workload blog published for the event) and “Monthly summary” (listed in the September 2026 feature summaries that the hero post links as what else is new this month). Both tiers can be filtered.
Suggested actions follow the status: GA → Evaluate now; Public preview → Pilot; everything else (coming soon, preview coming soon, private preview, not specified) → Watch.

“Potential relevance for Farmers Insurance” statements are suggested use cases only. They are not statements about Farmers’ environment, projects, systems or adoption, and no savings, ROI, performance or regulatory outcome is claimed.
gaps: Publication dates of the community blogs are not shown in the retrieved text (only relative ages), so announcement dates are given only for the hero and SQL blogs (2026-09-28).

community.fabric.microsoft.com, blog.fabric.microsoft.com and aka.ms short links block automated HTTP clients. Those pages were read in an integrated browser, and automated link checks cannot confirm them.

The monthly feature summaries list well over 150 items. This catalog groups related sub-capabilities into bundles and does not individually catalog minor user-interface changes; it is not claimed to be exhaustive.

Not found in Microsoft Learn “What’s new” at the cutoff: IQ sharing, Salesforce Data 360 integration, on-demand billing and zero-provisioned capacity, OneLake catalog in Excel and Foundry, F4096/F8192 SKUs, lakeFS shortcuts, and several others (see each card).
Database and Azure items were verified against the announcing blogs, with only a spot check of the Hyperscale documentation.
Microsoft Fabric roadmap pages, keynote and session recordings, and the Planning in Fabric and dedicated Data Factory posts were not reviewed.
Items with status “Not specified” give no availability label in the retrieved text; they can be listed with the status filter.

announcements.title: Fabric IQ in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Cowork
announcements.product: Fabric IQ; Microsoft Copilot; Power BI semantic models
announcements.summary: Governed Power BI reports and semantic models can now ground answers in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Cowork, so users get answers based on the same measures and definitions used in existing reports.
details: Announced as generally available for Copilot Chat and Cowork.
Copilot infers which report or semantic model fits the question; in Cowork, Power BI content can take part in long-running, asynchronous tasks.

Responses cite the Power BI content behind an answer and show the Microsoft Purview label applied to it; Power BI permissions and row-level security determine which content a user can reach (Power BI September feature summary).
Microsoft Purview DLP policies and information protection controls are supported for this experience (Power BI September feature summary).
The hero blog says customers get these insights “without additional AI token costs”. It does not say there are no license or capacity requirements.
announcements.announced: Generally available today (Copilot Chat and Cowork).
announcements.prereq: Licensing, capacity and tenant-setting requirements are not detailed in the retrieved announcement text. “No additional AI token costs” must not be read as free of license or capacity cost.
announcements.relevance: Business users could ask questions over certified claims, underwriting or finance semantic models in the flow of work, reusing existing definitions, row-level security and sensitivity labels.
announcements.next: Pick one certified semantic model and a small business group, compare Copilot answers with existing reports, and confirm licensing, tenant settings and data-protection posture with Microsoft.
announcements.theme: AI grounded in trusted enterprise data

announcements.title: Fabric IQ context in the new Copilot “Code” experience
announcements.summary: Fabric IQ business context is planned to reach the new Copilot Code experience for people who build their own solutions.
details: Described as “coming soon through the Frontier program”.
No date or availability tier is given.
announcements.announced: Coming soon through the Frontier program.
announcements.prereq: Frontier program participation is referenced. Other requirements are not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could extend governed business context to employees who build lightweight solutions with Copilot; early and program-gated.
announcements.next: Watch only; revisit when availability beyond the Frontier program is confirmed.

announcements.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot integrated into Power BI and Fabric
announcements.product: Microsoft 365 Copilot; Power BI; Fabric IQ; Work IQ
announcements.summary: A preview that brings Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat directly into Power BI and Fabric, combining Fabric data (through Fabric IQ) with Microsoft 365 work context (through Work IQ) in one conversation.
details: Shared conversation history lets users continue a discussion across Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences.
A Fabric admin portal setting controls the navigation entry point and is off by default.
The setting is independent of the existing standalone Power BI Copilot setting.
Support for Fabric users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license is described as following later, with a possibly different experience.
announcements.announced: Preview (Power BI September feature summary). Analytics and Power BI blogs describe the integration as “coming”.
announcements.prereq: During the initial preview, available only to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Controlled by an admin setting that is off by default.
announcements.conflict: The Analytics and Power BI blogs describe the integration as “coming”, while the Power BI September feature summary describes a preview rolling out with the admin setting off by default.
announcements.relevance: Analysts could combine report insights with emails, meetings and documents in one place, if the organization uses Microsoft 365 Copilot.
announcements.next: Pilot with a small licensed group once an admin decision on the tenant setting is made; confirm the Microsoft 365 Copilot license position first.

announcements.title: Fabric IQ MCP Server reaches general availability
announcements.summary: Creators can use the same conversational analytics in development environments and external MCP clients, with admin controls over which semantic models are available through Copilot.
details: Listed as “Fabric IQ MCP Server (Generally Available)” in the September feature summary.
Enhanced governance controls let organizations decide which semantic models are exposed.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could let approved developer tools and agents query governed semantic models without copying logic or data.
announcements.next: Test from a developer tool against a non-sensitive semantic model and review which models are exposed.

announcements.title: Governance controls for Copilot over Fabric data
announcements.product: Microsoft Purview; Power BI; Fabric admin
announcements.summary: Sensitivity labels, DLP policies and information protection now flow into Copilot experiences, and administrators can restrict which semantic models take part in AI experiences.
details: Analytics blog: sensitivity labels, DLP policies and information protection controls flow into Microsoft Copilot experiences.
“Restrict from Copilot” gives administrators control over which semantic models can participate in AI experiences.
The Power BI September feature summary lists “New control for Copilot access to semantic models” without a status label.
Microsoft 365 Copilot data answers over Power BI honor Purview DLP and information protection.
announcements.announced: Described as available; individual capabilities are not status-labelled in the retrieved text.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Gives security and data owners a way to decide which models are exposed to Copilot before broader rollout.
announcements.next: Inventory semantic models by sensitivity and decide default Copilot exposure with the governance team.

announcements.title: Fabric data agents generally available in Microsoft Copilot Studio
announcements.summary: Fabric data agents can be used from Microsoft Copilot Studio, with improvements in ontologies, relationship awareness and topic-aware guidance aimed at more complex production questions.
details: Learn lists “Fabric Data Agent integration with Microsoft Copilot Studio” as generally available.
announcements.announced: Generally available in Microsoft Copilot Studio.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Agents built in Copilot Studio could answer questions over governed Fabric data rather than separate extracts.
announcements.next: Prototype one narrowly scoped agent on a curated dataset and evaluate answer quality and access controls.
announcements.theme: AI grounded in trusted enterprise data

announcements.title: Data agent visualizations and MCP tasks
announcements.summary: Fabric data agents can return visualizations in answers and support Model Context Protocol tasks.
details: “Visualizations in the Fabric Data Agent (Generally Available)”.
“Microsoft Fabric data agent now supports Model Context Protocol tasks (Generally Available)”.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Richer answers could make data agents more usable for non-technical analysts.
announcements.next: Include in the data agent proof of concept.

announcements.title: Data agent context and quality improvements (preview)
announcements.summary: A set of preview enhancements to Fabric data agents covering topics, ontology as a context source, larger result sets, runtime model upgrades and feedback in Microsoft 365 Copilot.
details: Scale business context with Topics in Fabric data agents (Preview).
Ontology as context source (Preview).
Data agents return up to 1,000 rows (Preview).
Model upgrades on the data agent runtime (Preview).
Monitor and improve data agents with user feedback in Microsoft 365 Copilot (Preview).
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Business glossary context and feedback loops could improve how agents interpret insurance terminology.
announcements.next: Pilot topics and feedback on the same proof of concept; capture accuracy findings.

announcements.title: Build agent with AI mode uses semantic models, glossaries and data dictionaries
announcements.summary: The build agent with AI mode can use semantic models, documentation, glossaries and data dictionaries to generate richer data agent configurations with less manual effort.
details: The hero blog says the mode “can now use” these inputs without a status label; Learn lists “Build Agent with AI” as a preview feature.
announcements.announced: Described as available; status not stated in the hero blog.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could reduce effort to stand up domain agents using existing data dictionaries.
announcements.next: Try with an existing glossary or data dictionary to judge setup effort.

announcements.title: Fabric IQ answers from data agents and ontologies (preview)
announcements.product: Fabric IQ; Fabric data agents; ontologies
announcements.summary: Fabric IQ conversational analytics expands to include answers from data agents and ontologies.
details: Listed as “Expansion of Fabric IQ to include answers from data agents and ontologies (Preview)”.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could connect business concepts such as policy, claim and coverage to conversational answers.
announcements.next: Evaluate alongside the ontology pilot.

announcements.title: Agentic creation and conversational authoring of ontologies
announcements.summary: A new agentic experience creates ontologies from semantic models, OneLake data and other context documents, and ontologies can be built and queried conversationally.
details: Reduces the effort of capturing business concepts and relationships.
Related features in the September feature summary: build and query ontologies conversationally; bind faster and query at source scale.
announcements.announced: Introduced at the event; availability tier not stated in the retrieved text.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: A shared vocabulary for entities such as policyholder, policy, claim and adjuster could give agents and reports consistent business meaning.
announcements.next: Watch; confirm status, then test on a small, well-understood domain.
announcements.theme: AI grounded in trusted enterprise data

announcements.title: Power BI measures and natural-language rules in ontologies
announcements.summary: Power BI measures can be carried into an ontology, and rules can be defined in natural language and connected to entities, properties and relationships.
details: Lets established metrics be reused instead of redefined.
Related items: Ontology Metrics, Semantic Models as a data source, Ontology Rules.
announcements.announced: Introduced at the event; availability tier not stated.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Business rules such as coverage or reserve thresholds could be captured once and interpreted consistently by people and agents.
announcements.next: Watch; test with one governed metric after status is confirmed.

announcements.title: Ontology modelling at scale: RDF/OWL, namespaces, inheritance and versioning
announcements.summary: Enhancements for organizing and evolving large ontologies, including standards-based import/export, namespaces, type hierarchies and versioning.
details: RDF/OWL import and export.
Namespaces and type hierarchies with inheritance.
Relationships without joins and keyless entity bindings.
Built-in versioning and a full canvas experience.
announcements.announced: Listed in the September feature summary and the RTI/IQ blog; status not labelled.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Standards-based import/export could ease reuse of existing enterprise vocabularies.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: Governed ontology operations: security, APIs, CI/CD and MCP tools
announcements.summary: Ontology authoring and querying respect underlying data permissions, with management APIs, CI/CD support, an SDK and MCP tools for external agents.
details: OneLake security and row-level security respected in ontology authoring and querying.
Management APIs, CI/CD support and an Ontology Management SDK.
Ontology MCP tools for external agents and developer tools.
Graph data materialization can be enabled selectively.
Real-Time Dashboards with ontology as a source are listed as Preview in Learn.
announcements.announced: Listed in the RTI/IQ blog and September feature summary; status not labelled for most items.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Permission-aware, versionable ontologies fit regulated change management.
announcements.next: Watch; include in ontology evaluation criteria.

announcements.title: Semantic views: an early look at OneLake-native semantics
announcements.summary: An early look at semantic views, which define governed business metrics and semantics directly where data lives in OneLake and reuse them across Fabric and beyond.
details: Described as a “sneak peek” / “early look”; no availability date or tier is given.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could help keep metric definitions consistent across reports, applications and AI if it becomes available.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: Commitment to Apache Ossie (incubating) semantic metadata standard
announcements.product: Power BI semantic layer; Fabric IQ
announcements.summary: Microsoft affirmed its commitment to Apache Ossie, a community-led standard for exchanging semantic metadata across analytics, AI and BI platforms, working with Snowflake.
details: Collaboration with Snowflake currently focuses on cross-platform semantic-layer conversion.
Stated direction: establish DAX as an Ossie-recognized query language and expand support for ontologies.
announcements.announced: Commitment to a community standard; not a product release.
announcements.prereq: Not applicable; this is a standards commitment.
announcements.relevance: Open semantic metadata could reduce lock-in of business definitions across tools.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: Agentic app creation in Power BI Desktop (Apps in Power BI)
announcements.product: Power BI Desktop; Fabric Apps; SQL database in Fabric
announcements.summary: Starting from a trusted semantic model, users describe an application in natural language, preview and edit it, and publish it to Fabric. Apps can accept inputs, write back data, preserve shared state and support operational workflows.
details: Built on Fabric Apps, which provide each app with a SQL database in Fabric, authentication and security.
Hero blog: Apps in Power BI will be available in preview “in the coming weeks” to Power BI Pro, Premium Per User and Fabric capacity customers.
Power BI blog: the Desktop experience “will be available … in the coming months”.
Pro and Premium Per User customers are described as having access to Fabric Apps and Fabric Database capabilities “at no additional cost”, up to 1 GB per app (hero blog).
announcements.announced: Preview “in the coming weeks” (hero blog) / Desktop experience “in the coming months” (Power BI blog).
announcements.prereq: Power BI Pro, Premium Per User or Fabric capacity. Detailed licensing terms are not specified in the public sources.
announcements.conflict: Hero blog says preview “in the coming weeks”; the Power BI blog says “in the coming months” for Power BI Desktop. The Analytics blog says Fabric Apps “will be included with Power BI Pro”.
docs: Power BI’s next chapter (Fabric apps gallery link)
announcements.relevance: Could turn a dashboard that ends in a spreadsheet, such as a claims review or exception workflow, into a governed application with write-back.
announcements.next: Watch; shortlist one workflow and the semantic model it would start from, and review app governance with IT.

announcements.title: Fabric Apps: TypeScript backend functions, Secret Store and storage
announcements.summary: Fabric Apps adds server-side TypeScript functions, a Secret Store for credentials and built-in storage so apps can move from prototype toward production.
details: Functions run under the app identity and can forward signed-in user context; Fabric handles hosting, authentication, deployment and scaling.
Secret Store encrypts credentials and provides them to functions only at runtime.
Storage (folders, accepted file types, size limits and permissions) is defined in code.
Learn lists “Fabric Apps functions and connectors” and “Fabric Apps backend with the Rayfin SDK” as preview.
announcements.announced: Announced at the event; availability tier not stated in the Fabric Apps blog.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.conflict: The Fabric Apps blog says the initial launch was in June 2026; the OneLake blog says “Last May”.
announcements.relevance: Business-owned workflow apps could include custom rules and document attachments while staying on governed Fabric data.
announcements.next: Pilot with a low-risk internal workflow; review generated code and permissions as for any application.

announcements.title: Fabric Apps data connectors to Fabric data without copying
announcements.product: Fabric Apps; Fabric SQL database; Warehouse; Lakehouse; semantic models
announcements.summary: Apps connect directly to Fabric SQL databases, warehouses, Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoints and Power BI semantic models without duplicating data, preserving permissions and trusted measures.
details: SQL database and Warehouse support read and write; Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoints and semantic models are read-only.
With delegated authentication the connector runs as the signed-in user and the source enforces its own authorization, including row-level security.
Application identity does not inherit a user’s permission boundary and should be chosen deliberately.
announcements.announced: Announced at the event; availability tier not stated in the Fabric Apps blog.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Apps could reuse certified measures and respect row-level security rather than re-implementing logic.
announcements.next: Pilot with delegated authentication on a read-only semantic model.

announcements.title: Fabric Apps: PostgreSQL, private-by-default access, metrics and templates
announcements.summary: PostgreSQL support alongside SQL Server, private-by-default access, built-in usage and performance metrics, a Universal App template and a GitHub Copilot plugin.
details: Apps are private by default; Microsoft Entra authentication happens before any app content is delivered.
Builders can choose private, embedded-only or public access for approved anonymous scenarios; tenant-level controls govern exposure.
Built-in metrics: sign-ins, app loads, query volume, errors and average query duration.
Generated code is described as a starting point that still needs review, authorization checks and testing.
announcements.announced: Announced at the event; availability tier not stated.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Private-by-default design and built-in telemetry address common IT concerns about citizen-built applications.
announcements.next: Watch; include in the Fabric Apps governance review.

announcements.title: Fabric Apps planned for later in 2026
announcements.summary: Planned capabilities include an admin and security portal, Microsoft Copilot integration, app insights, a Kusto connector, app sharing with provenance, custom claims, OneLake-integrated storage, embedding and deployment pipelines.
details: The Power BI feature summary also lists support for Fabric Apps in Org apps as “Coming Soon”.
No dates are given.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: An admin portal and deployment pipelines would matter for governed rollout.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: Build Fabric Apps in the GitHub Copilot App
announcements.summary: A natural-language chat interface in the GitHub Copilot App plans, builds and deploys Fabric Apps on governed data.
details: The user reviews and approves a plan, then asks the agent to execute it and names the target workspace.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Developer-led prototypes could start from approved semantic models.
announcements.next: Pilot with developers if Fabric Apps are evaluated.

announcements.title: Power BI agentic development experiences
announcements.product: Power BI; Power BI Authoring MCP server
announcements.summary: BI developers can delegate model and report work to an agent, review the result and refine it, using the Power BI Authoring MCP server and Desktop Bridge CLI.
details: Listed as “Power BI Agentic Experiences (Generally Available)”.
A remote Power BI Authoring MCP server is listed separately as Preview.
Skills for modeling and report authoring are published in the microsoft/skills-for-fabric repository.
announcements.announced: Generally available (agentic experiences); remote authoring MCP server in preview.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could speed up semantic model and report modernization work under developer review.
announcements.next: Evaluate with a BI developer on a non-production model.

announcements.title: Power BI Projects (PBIP) generally available
announcements.summary: Power BI Projects, a text-based project format that supports source control, is listed as generally available.
details: Further details were not reviewed for this briefing.
announcements.announced: Generally available (Power BI September feature summary).
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Supports versioned, reviewable BI assets.
announcements.next: Evaluate within BI development standards.

announcements.title: Full-text search, string indexing and approximate distinct count in semantic models
announcements.summary: Preview modeling features: full-text search and string indexing for text searches, and approximate distinct count for Import and Direct Lake.
details: Introducing Full-Text Search in Power BI Semantic Models (Preview).
Accelerate text searches with String Indexing (Preview).
Approximate Distinct Count comes to Import and Direct Lake (Preview).
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Text search could help locate records in large claim-notes style datasets, if relevant.
announcements.next: Pilot only if a text-search use case exists.

announcements.title: IQ sharing for governed data and business context
announcements.summary: IQ sharing lets organizations share governed data and business context, such as Markdown agent instructions and RDF ontologies, across teams, customers and partners.
details: At launch it supports governed tables and files plus Markdown (.md) agent instructions and RDF (.rdf) ontologies.
Native support for Fabric IQ ontologies and Power BI semantic models is described as on the roadmap.
EY, S&P Global, TomTom, Financial Fabric and xMentium are described as building integrations; partner data products are discoverable through the OneLake catalog.
announcements.announced: Hero blog: “now in preview”. OneLake blog: “in preview soon”.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.conflict: The hero blog says IQ sharing is “now in preview”; the OneLake blog says “in preview soon”. It is not listed in Microsoft Learn at last check, so it is treated conservatively as preview coming soon.
announcements.relevance: Could support controlled sharing of data products and business definitions with internal domains or approved third parties, if such sharing is in scope.
announcements.next: Watch; confirm preview availability and sharing controls before scoping a use case.

announcements.title: Bidirectional integration between Salesforce Data 360 and OneLake
announcements.summary: Salesforce Data 360 data becomes available in OneLake through shortcuts without moving or duplicating it, including as context for Fabric data agents and ontologies.
details: Data is discoverable in the OneLake catalog and usable across SQL, notebooks and Power BI.
Queries use Fabric compute without placing load on Salesforce instances; Salesforce and OneLake security controls apply.
The hero blog calls this a “preview”; the OneLake blog does not restate the status in the retrieved text.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.conflict: Naming differs between sources (“Data Cloud 360” in the hero blog, “Data 360” in the OneLake blog).
announcements.relevance: Relevant only if Salesforce is part of the environment; this briefing makes no assumption either way.
announcements.next: Pilot only if Salesforce data is in scope.

announcements.title: Mirroring for Google BigQuery generally available
announcements.summary: Google BigQuery data can be mirrored into OneLake for analytics and AI with less duplication and fewer bespoke integrations.
details: Learn lists “Mirroring for Google BigQuery” as generally available.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Relevant only if BigQuery holds data of interest; no assumption is made about Farmers’ platforms.
announcements.next: Evaluate only if applicable.

announcements.title: Dynamics 365 Business Central mirroring into OneLake
announcements.summary: A new integration mirrors selected Business Central tables and company data into OneLake, with built-in monitoring for integration health.
details: The hero blog refers to “deeper integration with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central”.
announcements.announced: Announced; availability tier not stated in the retrieved text.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Relevant only if Business Central is used.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: OneLake shortcuts to versioned lakeFS data
announcements.summary: Shortcuts can reference the latest data of a lakeFS branch or a specific immutable commit, supporting reproducible reports, experiments and audits without copied snapshots.
announcements.announced: Announced; availability tier not stated in the retrieved text.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Versioned data access could support reproducible analyses, if lakeFS is used.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: Read and write OneLake data from Azure Databricks
announcements.summary: Azure Databricks can use OneLake data directly without copying it into another storage layer.
details: The OneLake blog says the capability is “now supported in production”.
Learn lists “Zero-copy access to OneLake data in Azure Databricks” as a preview feature.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.conflict: The OneLake blog says production support; Microsoft Learn lists the related feature as a preview. Treated conservatively as preview.
announcements.relevance: Could reduce duplicated storage across platforms, if Databricks is in use.
announcements.next: Pilot only if applicable; reconcile the status discrepancy with Microsoft first.

announcements.title: Apache Iceberg catalog federation for AWS Glue, Google and AVEVA CONNECT
announcements.summary: New Iceberg-based catalog federation support lets OneLake discover data registered in AWS Glue Data Catalog, the Google Lakehouse runtime catalog and AVEVA CONNECT.
announcements.announced: Announced; availability tier not stated in the retrieved text.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Open-format catalogs could reduce copying across clouds, if multiple clouds are used.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: OneLake Table APIs for agents, applications and engines
announcements.summary: A table read API gives agents and applications serverless access to Delta Lake and Iceberg tables without SQL, with OneLake security enforcing table, row and column access on every query.
details: Built on Apache Arrow.
Writing Iceberg tables to OneLake with Table APIs and credential vending is also listed as Preview.
Learn lists the OneLake table read API as a preview feature.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Governed, open-format table access for internal applications and agents without extracts.
announcements.next: Pilot with a non-sensitive table and review how security rules are enforced.
announcements.theme: Cross-platform data access and reduced duplication

announcements.title: OneLake engine ecosystem: ClickHouse, Teradata and LakeSail
announcements.summary: More external engines work with OneLake tables through open APIs and Iceberg support.
details: ClickHouse reading Apache Iceberg tables from OneLake through OneLake Table APIs is described as generally available.
A ClickHouse workload that provisions a dedicated ClickHouse Cloud service on Azure is described as public preview.
Teradata Autonomous Knowledge Platform integration lets Teradata users query OneLake tables in place through Iceberg APIs.
LakeSail brings Rust-native Spark-compatible processing for Delta Lake and Iceberg tables.
announcements.announced: Mixed: ClickHouse Iceberg reads GA; ClickHouse workload public preview; others not labelled in the retrieved text.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Shows OneLake acting as a shared data layer for several engines.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: OneLake catalog: browse tables and columns, preview data
announcements.summary: Users can explore individual tables and columns, view descriptions and preview data directly in the catalog, with filters for domains and tags.
details: The platform blog labels catalog exploration with quick actions, personalized views and filters as “(Generally Available)”.
Learn lists “OneLake Catalog table discovery” as a preview feature.
The September summary also lists object browsing and a new Global Search experience.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.conflict: The platform blog labels catalog exploration generally available; Learn lists table discovery as preview. Treated conservatively as preview.
announcements.relevance: Better discovery could reduce duplicate datasets and help analysts evaluate data before use.
announcements.next: Pilot with the data governance team; compare with current catalog tooling.

announcements.title: OneLake catalog search API, MCP and CLI tools
announcements.summary: Search returns relevance-ranked Fabric items, OneLake tables from lakehouses and mirrored sources, and semantic model tables in one result set, including for agents.
details: Described as agent-ready through a remote MCP server.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Programmatic discovery could support find-before-you-build practices.
announcements.next: Pilot with a developer team.

announcements.title: Spark granular runtime lineage in the OneLake catalog
announcements.summary: Granular runtime lineage for Spark is planned to show how data is used and transformed across the estate.
details: Described as “coming soon”; no date is given.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Lineage helps impact analysis and audit questions about where a number came from.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: OneLake catalog in Excel
announcements.summary: Business users can discover and analyze Fabric data in workbooks through the Get Data experience without copying the source data.
details: OneLake row- and column-level security and Microsoft Purview label-based protections apply.
announcements.prereq: Existing OneLake security and Purview protections apply.
announcements.relevance: Governed access to trusted data from a familiar tool for finance and actuarial analysts.
announcements.next: Pilot with a small analyst group.

announcements.title: OneLake catalog in Microsoft Foundry
announcements.summary: An embedded catalog gives a unified view across Fabric and Foundry so developers can find trusted data and add it to knowledge, agents and workflows.
details: Foundry users can see metadata, endorsements, sensitivity labels and descriptions before connecting OneLake items.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could ground custom AI applications in governed, labelled data.
announcements.next: Pilot if custom AI applications use Foundry.

announcements.title: Planning in Fabric stores planning data and writeback in OneLake
announcements.summary: Planning data and writeback can be stored directly in OneLake for larger models and more contributors.
details: The OneLake blog states planning performance and scale increase “by up to 10x”; no methodology is given in the retrieved text.
announcements.announced: Planning in Fabric is described as Preview.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could be relevant to finance planning and forecasting workflows; performance claim is unverified.
announcements.next: Pilot only if a planning use case exists.

announcements.title: Atlan integration with Fabric generally available
announcements.summary: Atlan’s native Fabric connector is generally available and adds deeper lineage across semantic models, measures, Spark workloads (through Fabric Platform Lineage APIs) and Dataflow Gen2.
details: OneLake shortcuts also let teams access Atlan context and Atlan lakehouses from Fabric.
announcements.prereq: Requires an Atlan subscription (third-party product).
announcements.relevance: Relevant only if Atlan is used or evaluated for data governance.
announcements.next: Evaluate only if applicable.

announcements.title: Partner workloads generally available in Fabric
announcements.product: Fabric Workload Hub; Esri; Telmai; Celonis; Spectral Core; Financial Fabric; IntuigenceAI
announcements.summary: Several partner workloads are described as generally available, extending analysis inside Fabric.
details: Esri ArcGIS Maps for Microsoft Fabric: mapping and spatial analysis, Stream Layers for real-time data.
Telmai Data Reliability: monitors OneLake tables for volume, schema, freshness and completeness changes.
Celonis Process Intelligence: process visualization and root-cause exploration.
Spectral Core Fabric Migration: guided database migration with SQL code translation and validation.
Financial Fabric Capital Markets DataHub and IntuigenceAI for Fabric.
announcements.announced: Generally available (each labelled in the OneLake blog).
announcements.prereq: Partner products; licensing and pricing are determined by each partner and are not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Data-reliability monitoring and spatial analysis could support claims and catastrophe-related analytics; process mining could inform claims workflow analysis.
announcements.next: Evaluate selected partners against existing tools.

announcements.title: Metropolis VoiceLake (partner preview)
announcements.summary: Normalizes supported communications data into a Fabric Lakehouse with ready-made Power BI reports and a semantic model.
announcements.prereq: Partner product; licensing not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could relate to contact-centre analytics; no assumption is made about existing systems.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: Mirroring for SharePoint Lists generally available
announcements.summary: SharePoint Lists can be continuously replicated into OneLake for analytics, reporting and AI.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Business-maintained lists could be brought into governed analytics without manual exports.
announcements.next: Evaluate for departmental lists.

announcements.title: Extended capabilities for Fabric Mirroring (Mirroring Views)
announcements.summary: Extended capabilities add more advanced replication options, including Mirroring Views that replicate source views and business logic into OneLake without extra pipelines.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Reduces pipeline work for replicating curated source views.
announcements.next: Evaluate against current replication patterns.

announcements.title: Snowflake security roles replication for Mirroring
announcements.summary: Source-defined Snowflake roles and permissions are replicated alongside mirrored data and translated into OneLake security, reducing manual rebuilding of access controls.
announcements.prereq: Applies to Mirroring for Snowflake.
announcements.relevance: Relevant only if Snowflake is used.
announcements.next: Pilot only if applicable.

announcements.title: OneLake security: redesigned “View users in role” experience
announcements.summary: A redesigned experience simplifies permission auditing: administrators see who can access a table and what data a user can see, and can assign or revoke roles from the same place.
details: Listed as “New OneLake security UX with Members and Data Tabs (Generally Available)”.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
docs: Create and manage OneLake security roles
announcements.relevance: Easier access reviews support audit readiness; this does not itself confer regulatory compliance.
announcements.next: Evaluate with security administrators.

announcements.title: Row- and column-level policy sync across Databricks, Snowflake and OneLake security
announcements.summary: An integration maps row- and column-level policies between Databricks, Snowflake and OneLake security so access controls stay consistent without recreating policies manually.
announcements.announced: Announced; availability tier not stated in the retrieved text.
announcements.prereq: Third-party integration; details not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Consistent policies across platforms matter if multiple engines access shared data.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: Copy job: change data capture, SCD Type 2 and audit columns
announcements.summary: Copy job can replicate only changes using CDC, keep history with built-in SCD Type 2, and add audit columns without custom code.
details: After the initial load, Copy job processes only changes captured since the previous successful run.
SCD Type 2 preserves history by creating a new row version when tracked values change.
Audit columns add operational metadata to support traceability and troubleshooting, including for Snowflake destinations.
announcements.prereq: Supported sources and destinations only; see documentation.
announcements.relevance: Incremental loads with history tracking suit finance and reporting datasets where changes over time matter.
announcements.next: Evaluate on one incremental source table.

announcements.title: Copy job connectors, monitoring and staging improvements
announcements.summary: A set of generally available Copy job improvements for sources, folders and operations.
details: Azure Database for PostgreSQL connector.
CDC from read-only Snowflake databases; Oracle CDC initial-load improvements; SQL CDC custom capture instance names.
Multi-folder copy into separate destination tables; SharePoint folders as source and destination.
Integration with workspace monitoring; custom staging database and schema for CDC and SCD Type 2.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Broader connector and monitoring coverage can simplify ingestion operations.
announcements.next: Evaluate when a relevant source is in scope.

announcements.title: Copy job integration with Eventstream
announcements.summary: Copy job can use Eventstream as a source and destination, connecting batch and streaming movement.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could unify batch and streaming ingestion patterns.
announcements.next: Pilot if streaming ingestion is planned.

announcements.title: Pipelines: Lakehouse maintenance activity and retry back-off
announcements.summary: Run vacuum and optimize on Lakehouse tables as a pipeline step, and use increasing delays between activity retries.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Orchestrated table maintenance and more resilient retries support reliable reporting pipelines.
announcements.next: Evaluate in an existing pipeline.

Richer pipeline monitoring in workspace monitoring.
Fabric Actions activity: authenticated calls to Fabric REST APIs from pipelines.
Business Actions activity: calls to systems such as Stripe, Twilio and Jira.
announcements.verNote: Learn lists the Business Actions activity as a preview feature; the other items were not matched (checked 2026-10-06).
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Dependency handling could replace brittle scheduling workarounds.
announcements.next: Pilot in a non-production workspace.

announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Self-service data preparation improvements for analysts.

announcements.summary: Preview capabilities for Dataflow Gen2, including upgrade tooling from Dataflow Gen1.

Dynamic expression editor for destinations; refresh details in the Monitoring hub.
Enhancements for upgrading Power BI Dataflows Gen1 to Dataflow Gen2 (CI/CD) and for mapping data flow transforms.
announcements.verNote: Learn lists dynamic warehouse schema, query-result backup and refresh details as preview features; other items were not matched (checked 2026-10-06).

details: The retrieved announcement text does not describe the feature further.

announcements.next: Evaluate with Fabric administrators.

announcements.title: Fabric data engineering agent (Project Osmos)
announcements.summary: An agent takes on long-running data engineering projects such as migrations, lakehouse modernization, performance optimization, complex ETL and data preparation within engineer-defined guardrails.
details: Engineers define the outcome and guardrails; the agent plans, executes, validates and refines work over hours or days, executing natively on Fabric Spark.
Tasks inherit workspace permissions so authorized team members can monitor and contribute.
Works across Fabric and developer tools including GitHub Copilot, VS Code, Codex and Claude Code.
Built on technology from Microsoft’s acquisition of Osmos.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could help staff large modernization or data-quality remediation efforts that are hard to prioritize, with engineers in control.
announcements.next: Pilot on a bounded, non-production migration or remediation task and review outputs carefully.

announcements.title: Materialized Lake Views generally available

details: Listed as generally available in Learn for September 2026.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could simplify curated claims, policy and finance layers with managed refresh and quality constraints.
announcements.next: Evaluate on one curated reporting layer.

announcements.title: Fabric Spark: Native Execution Engine and Runtime 2.0
announcements.summary: Fabric Spark continues to advance with the Native Execution Engine and Runtime 2.0, plus resource profiles, custom live pools and shortcut transformations.

The September summary describes Fabric Runtime 2.0 as powered by Apache Spark 4.1.

announcements.relevance: Performance gains for existing Spark workloads without code changes, as claimed by Microsoft.
announcements.next: Watch; benchmark on representative workloads before drawing conclusions.

announcements.title: Custom Live Pools generally available

Delegated management of live pools for workspace Members is a separate preview.
Startup-time figures are based on internal Microsoft testing and may vary.
announcements.prereq: Requires a paid Fabric capacity and an existing custom Spark pool.
announcements.relevance: More predictable start times for scheduled data preparation.
announcements.next: Evaluate for time-sensitive notebook schedules.

announcements.title: Native JSON acceleration in the Native Execution Engine
announcements.summary: Accelerated JSON file reads in Fabric Runtime 2.0 for Spark DataFrame and Spark SQL workloads.

announcements.prereq: Fabric Runtime 2.0.
announcements.relevance: Semi-structured telemetry or API payload ingestion could benefit.
announcements.next: Pilot on a JSON-heavy workload.

announcements.summary: A Python library and VS Code extension integration let coding agents such as GitHub Copilot CLI, Codex and Claude Code discover, edit, run and diagnose Fabric notebooks safely.
details: Operations validate target identity and confirm destructive changes before modifying remote state.
The VS Code extension exposes a local MCP server after explicit user approval.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could speed notebook development with human review retained.

details: No dates are given.

announcements.relevance: Zero-copy access patterns for warehouse data.
announcements.next: Watch.

Distributed Bitmap Filters filter irrelevant rows before large joins.

announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.

Scalar UDFs usable across more query patterns.

announcements.title: Fabric expanding to Microsoft 365 GCC High
announcements.summary: Fabric is expanding to U.S. sovereign cloud customers in Microsoft 365 GCC High.
details: The platform blog cites frameworks such as DoD Impact Level 4, CJIS, DFARS and NIST 800-171.
announcements.prereq: Applies to Microsoft 365 GCC High customers.
announcements.relevance: Likely limited relevance unless U.S. government workloads are in scope.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: Unified workspace monitoring across workspaces
announcements.summary: Telemetry from multiple workspaces can be consolidated into one Eventhouse, with control over retention and caching, a custom endpoint for external destinations and API-based onboarding.
details: Most Fabric items are available at launch, with additional workloads over time.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Cross-workspace telemetry supports operational reliability and audit investigations.
announcements.next: Pilot with one domain’s workspaces.

announcements.title: Refreshed Monitor hub with health overview, capacity view and job alerts
announcements.summary: Ready-made views across workloads, jobs, apps, agents, alerts and capacities, with a health overview, capacity headroom and Activator-powered alerts for job successes and failures.
details: A Monitor item is described as a single management unit across capacities and the tenant.
The Activator-powered job alerts carry no separate status label in the platform blog.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Earlier detection of failing jobs and capacity pressure, supporting reliability.
announcements.next: Pilot with the platform operations team.
announcements.theme: Security, governance, reliability and cost management

announcements.title: Operations agents: investigation, performance view and pre-approved actions
announcements.product: Real-Time Intelligence operations agent; Fabric Observability Insights
announcements.summary: Operations agents investigate end-to-end causes, develop evidence-backed hypotheses, assess impact and recommend next steps, with human oversight; pre-approved actions and a performance view are added.
details: Currently helps investigate pipeline failures, with further support planned.
Investigator insights and the operations agent performance view are labelled Preview.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Faster root-cause analysis for data pipeline failures.
announcements.next: Pilot on pipeline failures with approvals kept manual.

announcements.title: On-demand billing and Fabric zero-provisioned (F0)
announcements.summary: Pay only for compute used, with automatic scaling, and start with Fabric and OneLake without an upfront capacity commitment.
details: The platform blog says on-demand billing is “in preview soon” and the capabilities “will be available in the coming weeks”.
OneLake compute on-demand billing is described as preview in the coming weeks.
The hero blog describes on-demand billing without a status.
announcements.prereq: Pricing and terms are not specified in the public sources; no savings are implied.
announcements.conflict: The hero blog describes the capability without a preview or timing label; the platform and OneLake blogs say preview in the coming weeks.
announcements.relevance: Consumption-based options could influence capacity strategy; economics are not stated.
announcements.next: Watch; request pricing and preview timing from Microsoft.

announcements.title: Workspace-level surge protection
announcements.summary: Set a workspace consumption limit to isolate runaway or non-critical workloads and protect mission-critical ones, with exemptions for critical workspaces.
details: The platform blog says it “will be generally available soon”.
Learn lists workspace-level surge protection as a preview feature.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.conflict: The platform blog heading says generally available soon; Learn lists it as preview as of the research cutoff.
announcements.relevance: Limits the impact of a runaway workload on shared capacity.
announcements.next: Pilot on a non-critical workspace; track GA.

announcements.title: Capacity overage and F4096/F8192 SKUs generally available
announcements.summary: Capacity overage allows additional paid compute with configured spending thresholds and notifications instead of sizing for rare peaks; F4096 and F8192 SKUs extend options for larger workloads.
announcements.verNote: Learn lists capacity overage as generally available; the F4096 and F8192 SKUs were not matched in Learn (checked 2026-10-06).
announcements.prereq: Charges and thresholds are not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Cost-control option for peak periods; the cost effect depends on actual usage and is not quantified.
announcements.next: Evaluate with the capacity owner.
announcements.theme: Security, governance, reliability and cost management

announcements.title: Capacity Metrics app enhancements
announcements.summary: Investigate health-state duration, capacity units per second, daily and hourly heatmaps and top item contributors, with chargeback app integration.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Supports usage allocation and cost transparency.
announcements.next: Evaluate with capacity administrators.

announcements.title: Capacity overview events and ready-made capacity alert templates
announcements.summary: Capacity overview events in Real-Time hub and templates for creating capacity alerts quickly.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Proactive capacity alerting.
announcements.next: Evaluate.

announcements.title: Capacity operation events and Capacity Insights & Actions
announcements.summary: Operation events add workspace- and item-level visibility, and Capacity Insights & Actions lets administrators adjust surge and overage settings, migrate workspaces or resize capacity.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Action-oriented capacity management.
announcements.next: Pilot with capacity administrators.

announcements.title: Deployment plans as workspace items
announcements.summary: Define deployment order on a visual canvas with YAML as source of truth, including pre- and post-deployment steps such as running a notebook or validating data.
details: The plan follows the solution through Git branch-out, sync, deployment pipelines and bulk import.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Repeatable, reviewable promotion between environments.
announcements.next: Pilot on a non-production solution.

announcements.title: Git integration: branch workspaces, selective branching and compare-and-commit
announcements.summary: Branch workspace, selective branching, change comparison and commits, and branched workspace relationships are generally available.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Clearer source-control workflows for analytics teams.
announcements.next: Evaluate with BI and data engineering teams.

announcements.title: Git integration previews: branch workspace admin profile, file-level commit, contributor branch switching
announcements.summary: Administrators define a profile applied to developer-created branch workspaces; developers can commit only ready files and switch the connected branch when enabled.
announcements.prereq: Contributor branch switching requires an administrator to enable it.
announcements.relevance: Self-service branching under admin guardrails.
announcements.next: Pilot.

announcements.title: Bulk item definition import/export APIs and higher API limits
announcements.summary: Move multiple item definitions in one call, with automatic deployment order and reference updates, supporting workspace-as-code, CI/CD and migration.
details: A unified quota model and increased limits for core APIs are described without a status.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Supports automated environment promotion.
announcements.next: Evaluate in a CI/CD pipeline.

announcements.title: Fabric Core MCP Server generally available
announcements.summary: A remote MCP server exposes Fabric core operations to AI tools.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Agent-assisted administration under existing permissions.
announcements.next: Evaluate in a developer sandbox.

announcements.title: OneLake catalog discovery in GitHub Copilot CLI through Skills for Fabric
announcements.product: Skills for Fabric; GitHub Copilot CLI
announcements.summary: Developers can find Fabric items and tables from the CLI before writing code, supporting a find-before-you-build approach.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Encourages reuse of governed data.
announcements.next: Evaluate with developers.

announcements.title: Database Hub in Fabric
announcements.product: Fabric Database Hub; SQL Server; Azure SQL; PostgreSQL; Azure Cosmos DB; SQL database in Fabric
announcements.summary: A centralized control plane to monitor health, assess risk, enforce governance and gain visibility across a database estate.
details: Brings together inventory, health, performance, security, risk and optimization signals.
The September summary lists Azure SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance, SQL Server on Azure VMs, Arc-enabled SQL Server, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Azure Cosmos DB and Fabric SQL database.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: A single view of a mixed database estate could support risk, performance and governance reviews.
announcements.next: Pilot with a representative set of databases.
announcements.theme: Security, governance, reliability and cost management

announcements.title: Database agents for SQL and PostgreSQL on Azure
announcements.product: Database Hub; Azure SQL; Azure Database for PostgreSQL; VS Code
announcements.summary: AI-powered agents observe database signals and help administrators investigate issues, find optimization opportunities and recommend actions within guardrails.
details: Preview begins with SQL in Database Hub and PostgreSQL in Visual Studio Code, with capabilities coming to both over time.
Agents operate within existing role-based access controls, approvals and auditing.
announcements.announced: Hero blog: “will soon be available in preview”. SQL blog and September summary: preview.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.conflict: The hero blog says the agents “will soon be available in preview”; the SQL blog, September summary and Learn describe a preview.
announcements.relevance: Could speed DBA troubleshooting; human judgment remains central as stated by Microsoft.
announcements.next: Pilot in a non-production environment.

announcements.title: Azure SQL Database Hyperscale: 160 and 192 vCore service objectives generally available
announcements.summary: More compute for demanding workloads.
details: The hero blog cites 192 vCore; the SQL blog says 160 and 192 vCore Premium-series objectives.
Microsoft Learn’s Hyperscale page lists up to 192 vCores and up to 128 TB.

The SQL blog cites a Microsoft-commissioned independent study with up to 50 percent better price-performance than Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL under the tested conditions; results should not be generalized.
announcements.verNote: Learn’s Hyperscale documentation lists up to 192 vCores (checked 2026-10-06).
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Headroom for large relational workloads, if Azure SQL is used.
announcements.next: Evaluate sizing for relevant workloads.

announcements.title: Hyperscale serverless auto-pause
announcements.summary: Compute pauses automatically when idle and resumes when workloads return, aimed at development, test and intermittent workloads.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Potential cost reduction for non-production databases; no savings are quantified.
announcements.next: Pilot on dev/test databases.

announcements.title: Higher-density Hyperscale elastic pools
announcements.summary: Elastic pool density increases to up to 50 databases per pool.
details: The SQL blog says higher-density elastic pools are in preview; the hero blog does not state a status.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: More consolidation options for many small databases.
announcements.next: Pilot if applicable.

announcements.title: DiskANN vector indexes generally available
announcements.product: Azure SQL Database Hyperscale; Azure SQL Managed Instance; SQL database in Fabric
announcements.summary: High-performance vector search inside the database engine for semantic search, recommendations and retrieval-augmented generation without a separate vector store.
details: The SQL blog says the vector index has full DML support and stays updated in real time.
announcements.verNote: Learn lists vector indexes and vector search in SQL database in Fabric as generally available; other engines were not matched (checked 2026-10-06).
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could ground RAG applications in operational data without moving it to a separate vector store.
announcements.next: Evaluate in a prototype.

announcements.title: Azure Arc migration experience for Hyperscale
announcements.product: Azure Arc; Azure SQL Database Hyperscale
announcements.summary: A centralized workflow for assessment, provisioning, migration, validation and cutover to Hyperscale.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could structure database migration projects, if applicable.
announcements.next: Pilot only if a migration is planned.

announcements.title: SQL Server on Azure Local generally available (connected and disconnected)
announcements.product: SQL Server; Azure Local; Azure Arc
announcements.summary: Run SQL Server on Azure Local in customer-controlled environments, with Azure management for connected deployments and a local control plane for disconnected operations.
details: Supports SQL Server workloads on Windows Server or Linux virtual machines.

Licensing: SQL Server is licensed separately from Azure Local; connected deployments can use eligible existing licenses or pay-as-you-go through Azure Arc; disconnected deployments use eligible licenses through Azure Hybrid Benefit (SQL Server blog).
announcements.prereq: Separate SQL Server licensing applies; see the SQL Server blog.
announcements.relevance: Relevant if workloads must stay in customer-controlled environments; this briefing makes no assumption about Farmers’ needs.
announcements.next: Evaluate only where on-premises control requirements exist.

announcements.title: Foundry Local on Azure Local
announcements.summary: Run AI models close to data in customer-controlled environments.
announcements.prereq: Requires Azure Local.
announcements.relevance: Relevant only for AI that must stay in controlled environments.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: GitHub Copilot Agent Mode in SSMS, SQL Projects and Schema Compare generally available
announcements.product: SQL Server Management Studio; Visual Studio Code
announcements.summary: Agent Mode helps developers reason across database objects and complete multistep tasks; SQL Projects and Schema Compare are generally available in SSMS, plus SQL Formatter in SSMS and VS Code.
announcements.prereq: Requires GitHub Copilot access.
announcements.relevance: Developer productivity and source control for database changes.
announcements.next: Evaluate with DBAs and database developers.

announcements.title: Data API builder: vector and JSON support
announcements.summary: Connects SQL data to applications and agents through REST, GraphQL and MCP endpoints, with vector and JSON support added.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
announcements.relevance: Could expose governed database content to applications and agents.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: Cosmos DB mirroring supports virtual network data gateways
announcements.summary: Mirroring can connect to Azure Cosmos DB accounts secured by private endpoints or virtual networks through a gateway running in the customer’s virtual network.
details: Public network access can stay disabled.
announcements.prereq: Requires a virtual network data gateway.
announcements.relevance: Mirroring for network-isolated Cosmos DB, if used.
announcements.next: Watch.

announcements.title: Change Event Streaming for SQL database in Fabric
announcements.summary: Streams committed row-level changes in near real time as CloudEvents-style JSON, using transaction-log capture without polling or connectors.
announcements.prereq: Not specified in the public source.
docs: Stream SQL change events to Eventstream
announcements.relevance: Near-real-time operational signals from application databases.
announcements.next: Pilot if real-time data is planned.
